$schema_note: Curated dataset of evidence-ranked actions. See docs/METHODOLOGY.md for field definitions, the confidence scale, and how 'score' is derived. Every impact figure must carry at least one source with an access date.

actions.title: Donate $10 to a top-rated malaria charity

impact.metric: expected fraction of a life saved
impact.explanation: GiveWell estimates roughly $3,000-$5,500 to save a life via its top charities; insecticide-treated nets cost about $5 each, so $10 buys ~2 nets and roughly 1/500th of a statistical life saved.

sources.name: GiveWell — How much does it cost to save a life?

actions.title: Fund vitamin A supplements for children

impact.explanation: Vitamin A supplementation costs roughly $1-2 per child per round and reduces child mortality; GiveWell funded Helen Keller Intl programs at an estimated ~$3,500 per life saved (2022-2024 average).

sources.name: GiveWell blog — How we're searching for the best ways to help in 2026

actions.title: Fund school deworming treatments

impact.explanation: Mass school-based deworming costs well under $1 per child per year. Long-term studies suggest income gains for treated children, though the size of developmental effects is debated among researchers.

actions.title: Send cash directly to a family in extreme poverty

impact.explanation: GiveDirectly delivers roughly $0.80 of every donated dollar to households in extreme poverty. Dozens of RCTs show cash transfers increase earnings, assets and wellbeing; GiveWell uses cash as its benchmark intervention.

actions.title: Fund safe drinking water chlorination

impact.explanation: Chlorine dispenser programs cost on the order of $1.50 per person per year. GiveWell has directed over $150M to water chlorination as among the most cost-effective water interventions, though 2026 coverage surveys flagged adherence concerns in some programs.

actions.title: Donate $10 to a vetted high-leverage climate charity

impact.explanation: Evaluators like Giving Green and Founders Pledge estimate their top climate recommendations avert CO2 at single-digit dollars per tonne — far cheaper than most personal offsets. Estimates are inherently uncertain and vary widely by charity.

actions.title: Fund sight-restoring cataract surgery

impact.metric: fraction of a cataract surgery funded
impact.explanation: In some low-income countries, sight-restoring cataract surgery can be delivered for roughly $25-$100 (The Fred Hollows Foundation cites as little as $25 in some programs). Restored sight transforms independence and earning ability.

actions.title: Fund depression treatment in low-income countries

impact.explanation: Group interpersonal therapy delivered by lay counselors (e.g. StrongMinds) treats depression for roughly $100-$250 per person. Wellbeing-focused evaluators rate this highly, though cost and effect estimates vary between analyses.

actions.title: Fund the fight against childhood lead poisoning

impact.explanation: Lead exposure damages children's cognitive development at massive scale. Advocacy for lead-paint regulation (e.g. LEEP) is rated among the most cost-effective interventions by external evaluators because small budgets can change national policy.

actions.title: Donate $10 to your local food bank

impact.explanation: Feeding America states each $1 helps provide about 10 meals through its network — a figure that leverages donated food and bulk purchasing, so it measures distribution leverage rather than retail value.

actions.title: Donate blood

impact.explanation: The American Red Cross states a single donation can help save more than one life because blood is separated into red cells, plasma and platelets; someone in the U.S. needs blood roughly every 2 seconds.

sources.name: American Red Cross — Importance of the blood supply

actions.title: Donate platelets

impact.explanation: Platelets are critical for cancer patients in chemotherapy and shelf-stable for only about 5-7 days, so supply is perpetually short. One apheresis donation can provide a full transfusable dose.

actions.title: Register as an organ donor

impact.explanation: HRSA states one organ donor can save up to 8 lives and enhance dozens more through tissue donation. Only a small fraction of deaths permit donation, so the expected value per registrant is far below 8 — but the cost is 2 minutes.

actions.title: Join the bone marrow / stem cell registry

impact.explanation: Registering is a cheek swab; roughly 1 in 430 U.S. registry members ever donate. But for a blood-cancer patient without a family match, a registry match can be the only curative option.

sources.name: NMDP (Be The Match) — Likelihood of donating

actions.title: Take a CPR course

impact.metric: survival multiplier when CPR is given promptly
impact.explanation: The AHA states CPR, especially if performed immediately, can double or triple survival from out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (~350,000 U.S. cases/year); a 2024 JAHA study found 81% greater survival odds when bystander CPR starts within 2 minutes.

sources.name: American Heart Association — What is CPR
JAHA — Witnessed arrest vs bystander CPR (2024)

actions.title: Take a Stop the Bleed course

impact.explanation: Uncontrolled bleeding is a leading cause of preventable death after trauma; a person can bleed out in under 5 minutes, before responders arrive. The 90-minute course teaches tourniquets and wound packing.

sources.name: American College of Surgeons — Stop the Bleed

actions.title: Volunteer a shift at a food bank

impact.explanation: Independent Sector values a U.S. volunteer hour at $36.14 (2026). Food bank sorting shifts are high-leverage because volunteer labor lets the food bank's dollars go to food instead of payroll.

sources.name: Independent Sector — Value of volunteer time 2026

actions.title: Tutor a struggling student weekly

impact.metric: standard deviations of learning gain (high-dosage tutoring)
impact.explanation: A meta-analysis of 96 RCTs found tutoring programs raise achievement by ~0.37 standard deviations on average — one of the largest effects of any education intervention. Consistency matters more than credentials.

sources.name: Nickow, Oreopoulos & Quan (NBER w27476) — The impressive effects of tutoring

actions.title: Train as a crisis line volunteer

impact.metric: people in crisis supported per weekly shift
impact.explanation: Crisis lines like Crisis Text Line and 988 depend on trained volunteers; evaluations show most texters report their conversation helped. Training is substantial (~30 hours) but the ongoing weekly commitment reaches many people in acute distress.

actions.title: Mentor a young person

impact.explanation: RCTs of Big Brothers Big Sisters found mentored youth were significantly less likely to start using drugs and skipped fewer school days. Effects are real but modest; long-term consistent matches matter most.

actions.title: Donate your professional skills pro bono

impact.metric: value of skilled volunteer time (USD/hour, lower bound)
impact.explanation: The general volunteer hour is valued at $36.14 (2026); specialized skills (design, legal, accounting, code) are worth several times that to a nonprofit that would otherwise pay market rates or go without.

sources.name: Independent Sector — Value of volunteer time 2026

actions.title: Help at a voter registration drive

impact.explanation: Nonpartisan registration drives measurably increase turnout among those registered. The civic value of marginal registrations is hard to quantify, so we grade this low-confidence despite clear mechanism.

sources.name: League of Women Voters — Voter registration

actions.title: Volunteer to read with children at a library or school

impact.explanation: Shared reading builds vocabulary and print familiarity; meta-analyses find consistent positive effects of shared-reading interventions on early language outcomes, with the largest benefits for children with fewer books at home.

actions.title: Ask someone directly if they're thinking about suicide

impact.explanation: A meta-analysis (Dazzi et al. 2014, Psychological Medicine) found asking about suicide does NOT increase suicidal ideation — and may reduce it. Asking directly and connecting someone to help (call/text 988 in the U.S.) is an evidence-backed act of courage.

sources.name: Dazzi et al. 2014 — Does asking about suicide induce suicidal ideation? (Psychological Medicine)

actions.title: Intervene when you witness harassment (the 5 Ds)

impact.metric: share of situations where intervention helps
impact.explanation: In naturalistic playground observations, 57% of peer interventions stopped bullying episodes. Trainings like Right To Be's '5 Ds' (Distract, Delegate, Document, Delay, Direct) give bystanders safe options short of confrontation.

sources.name: Hawkins, Pepler & Craig 2001 — Naturalistic observations of peer interventions (Social Development)
Right To Be — The 5 Ds of bystander intervention

actions.title: Take the keys from someone about to drive impaired

impact.metric: share of U.S. traffic deaths involving alcohol
impact.explanation: Roughly a third of U.S. traffic fatalities (~13,000+ people/year) involve an alcohol-impaired driver (NHTSA). An awkward conversation and a rideshare fare is one of the cheapest life-risk reductions an ordinary person can buy.

actions.title: Speak up about a mistake or safety risk at work

impact.metric: relative error reduction from speaking-up cultures
impact.explanation: Patient-safety research consistently links psychological safety and speaking-up behavior with fewer adverse events; surgical checklist and speak-up programs show measurable harm reductions. Effect sizes vary by setting, hence medium confidence.

sources.name: AHRQ PSNet — Speaking up for patient safety

actions.title: Report fraud or wrongdoing you have evidence of

impact.metric: dollars recovered by whistleblower programs (cumulative, USD billions)
impact.explanation: The SEC's whistleblower program alone has led to billions of dollars in sanctions and investor recoveries since 2011. Whistleblowing carries real personal risk — the highest courage rating on this site — which is exactly why it's on the list.

actions.title: Regularly check on an isolated neighbor or relative

impact.explanation: Holt-Lunstad's meta-analysis of 148 studies (~309,000 people) found lacking social connection carries a mortality risk comparable to smoking up to 15 cigarettes a day. Regular human contact for an isolated person targets a genuinely large health risk.

sources.name: Holt-Lunstad et al. 2010 — Social relationships and mortality risk (PLOS Medicine)

actions.title: Stand up for someone being bullied

impact.metric: share of peer interventions that stop bullying
impact.explanation: In observed school bullying episodes, peers were present 88% of the time but intervened in only 19% — yet when they did intervene, 57% of interventions stopped the bullying. The gap between presence and action is the opportunity.

sources.name: Hawkins, Pepler & Craig 2001 — Naturalistic observations of peer interventions (Social Development)

actions.title: Take a Mental Health First Aid course

impact.explanation: Meta-analyses find MHFA training improves mental-health literacy, reduces stigma, and increases helping behaviors toward people in distress. Evidence for downstream outcomes in those helped is thinner, hence medium confidence.

actions.title: Apologize sincerely and repair a relationship you damaged

impact.explanation: Experimental research finds apologies that take responsibility and offer repair substantially increase forgiveness and relationship restoration versus no apology or partial apologies. Effects on long-run wellbeing are less quantified.

sources.name: Greater Good Science Center — The science of apologies

actions.title: Have the end-of-life wishes conversation with your family

impact.metric: reduction in family distress and unwanted care
impact.explanation: Advance care planning trials show fewer unwanted aggressive interventions and less anxiety/depression in surviving relatives when wishes were discussed in advance. One brave dinner conversation spares a family the worst version of its hardest week.

actions.title: Swap one beef meal per week for plants

impact.explanation: Beef emits ~60 kg CO2e per kg (Poore & Nemecek 2018 via Our World in Data) versus ~1-2 kg for beans. Swapping ~250g of beef weekly avoids roughly 0.7 tonnes CO2e per year — one of the largest single-food levers.

sources.name: Our World in Data — GHG per kg of food product (Poore & Nemecek)
Our World in Data — Environmental impacts of food

actions.title: Wash laundry in cold water

impact.metric: share of washer energy used for heating water
impact.explanation: About 90% of a washing machine's energy goes to heating water (ENERGY STAR). Cold washes cut that almost entirely, clean modern detergents fine, and save money — a rare zero-effort habit with a real number behind it.

actions.title: Set up a small recurring donation to an effective charity

impact.explanation: Automation beats intention: recurring donors give substantially more over time than one-off donors with identical intentions. $5/month to a GiveWell top charity is ~$60/year — about 1-2% of a statistical life saved, every year, on autopilot.

actions.title: Try pledging 1% of income to effective charities

impact.metric: annual giving at 1% of median U.S. income (approx. USD)
impact.explanation: Giving What We Can's Trial Pledge (1%+ of income) turns generosity into a standing commitment. At a $60k income that's $600/year — enough to fully fund vitamin A supplementation for hundreds of children annually.

sources.name: Giving What We Can — Trial Pledge

actions.title: Cut your household food waste

impact.metric: share of global GHG emissions from food loss and waste
impact.explanation: UNEP estimates food loss and waste accounts for roughly 8-10% of global greenhouse gas emissions; U.S. households also lose real money to it. Meal planning and freezing are the highest-leverage fixes.

actions.title: Repair things instead of replacing them

impact.explanation: Electronic waste is the world's fastest-growing waste stream (UN Global E-waste Monitor), and most of a device's emissions are embodied in manufacturing. Repair cafés and iFixit guides make repair genuinely accessible.

actions.title: Walk or bike trips under 2 miles

impact.metric: share of U.S. car trips under ~3 miles
impact.explanation: Roughly half of U.S. car trips are under three miles (U.S. DOT travel surveys) — the distance range where walking or cycling is most practical. The swap pays a double dividend: avoided emissions plus the well-documented health benefits of routine activity.

sources.name: U.S. DOT Bureau of Transportation Statistics — Trip length distributions

actions.title: Send one genuine appreciation message a week

impact.explanation: Studies of gratitude letters find senders underestimate how much recipients appreciate them, and expression modestly boosts both parties' mood. The evidence base is mixed on durability, so we grade this low — it stays on the list because the cost is nearly zero.
